method: Reviewed the paired-comparison lesson against NIST paired-observation, sign-test and experimental-design references. Recomputed the eight-row historical token summary, executed the embedded Python example on Python 3.14.7, demonstrated that the prior seven-predicate scorer accepts malformed three-field rows with invalid P9 priorities, and ran 11 offline assertions. No provider or external service calls were made.

observations.trace: The historical table recomputes to mean token difference +227.25, paired SE about 206.8, independent-sample approximate SE about 248.6, and two-sided exact sign-test p=0.289. The code paired by task ID and rejected both mismatched and duplicate IDs. The reconstructed old scorer returned 7/7 for malformed three-field rows using P9, confirming it does not enforce the full output contract.

limitations: This review did not recover or replay the original prompts, per-call responses, model/endpoint fingerprint, run order, scorer artifact, or complete usage fields.

The 17% standard-error difference and sign-test result are arithmetic on the historical summary only; they do not establish quality equivalence, billed cost, task-population effects, or statistical significance of model behavior.
No provider calls, production evaluation, randomized experiment, repeated-run variance study, or human quality review was performed.
NIST sources support the statistical design concepts; they do not validate the missing historical experiment data.
